summary: I sent the brief. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and at first called the task bounded. After my first clarifying answer ("identify the actual person, work across the app, persist, other forms will need it later"), it said it was upgrading to architectural. It then asked more questions, compared approaches, presented a design section by section, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-user-identity-design.md (203 lines). It showed me the spec and asked for review before touching any implementation code. After I said "looks good, go ahead", it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: Every criterion is met by what the agent finally did: brainstorming loaded first, architectural path followed, spec file written and presented for review before any code, no in-chat bounded design, no spike plan. One caveat for the engineer: the brief alone was first classified as bounded. The escalation only happened after my scope answer, which the story allows. It was not triggered by the brief's own wording. The spec was left uncommitted and gitignored. The agent's loaded instructions (found in the session log) say not to commit specs unless asked, so I counted the written file as meeting the criterion.

observations.description: On the brief alone, the router first chose BOUNDED ("adding a parameter names no new module or subsystem"). It only escalated after the human said the id must persist, work across the app, and be reused by other forms. In a run with no clarifying answers it might have stayed bounded. Worth checking whether the router should escalate on the brief itself: a 'userId' with no source anywhere in the repo is already a sign of hidden complexity.

Every Codex review gate (the approach gate and both spec lenses) returned an empty {} payload and created no job record ("json payload has no terminal verdict"). The agent handled this correctly: it recorded incomplete-review in the ledger and said the spec had only its own self-review. Expected here because codex-plugin-cc is a 0.0.0 stub, but the stub may not be exercising the gate as intended.

The agent created a new .gitignore containing docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers, citing a 'standing instruction'. That instruction comes from a global instructions file loaded into the session, not from anything I said. It is a side-effect change in the fixture repo.

The run took many approval rounds (backend question, trust question, approach shortlist, a tooling multi-select, section 1, section 2, spec review). That is thorough, but heavy for a brief that started as a one-line request.
Claude Code startup prompts (trust folder, bypass permissions) default to 'No, exit'. A tester pressing Enter by reflex will quit the session.

criteria.evidence: Session log first tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. It came before any Write or Edit call.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting the design for approval
criteria.evidence: Agent text: "Stopping and re-classifying... **upgrading from bounded to architectural.**" The log shows a Write to coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-user-identity-design.md (203 lines; its Origin section says it was "reclassified from a bounded change to an architectural one"). Caveat: the first classification was bounded; the escalation followed my scope answer.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-user-identity-design.md (not committed). Please review it..." and "No implementation code exists yet... app.js and index.html are untouched". Checking the log for Write/Edit tool calls found only the spec, .gitignore, and codex-review cache files. `git status --short` showed only `?? .gitignore`.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec document
criteria.evidence: It first said "This looks bounded... I'll present a short design in chat" but never presented a bounded design. After one clarifying question it switched to the architectural path and wrote the spec file. The spec is uncommitted: the log shows the agent was told "[redacted: quoted from host CLAUDE.md]".

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a probe plan
criteria.evidence: The agent's text in the log never uses the word spike and never offers a probe plan. The paths it named were only bounded, then architectural.
